forced.why: The combat_skill line only speaks accuracy, damage %, move, launch/target and use-limits. Any resistance, DoT, conditional modifier, stress/heal scaling or persistent stat must be fired as a named effect the skill lists via .effect.
To reach a resistance, a rule-gated stat, or any non-combat-stat stat_type, the effect must apply a named buffs.json entry through .buff_ids — the skill->effect->buff bridge.
One combat_skill line exists per level 0-4; the raw .atk/.dmg/.crit live on each line and must be authored (vanilla keeps them static across all 5 levels).

choices.detail: A plain unconditional combat-stat swing (e.g. +8% dodge for the battle) can use inline .combat_stat_buff with no buffs.json entry; reach for .buff_ids only when you need a rule gate, a resistance, or a wider stat_type.
Escalation across ranks is authored by swapping WHICH effect the line fires at rank 3 vs rank 5, not by changing the static atk/dmg on the line.
A buff in the effect's .buff_ids unlocks all 55 rule_type gates (hpbelow, in_mode, monsterType, at_deaths_door...) plus is_false_rule inversion — the only route to conditional skill powers.
combat_move_skill and riposte_skill share the grammar; a Move slot can be turned into a stance toggle via .move 0 0 plus a .set_mode effect (Thorn/Cook pattern).
The .info's crit: .effects fires author-chosen effects whenever the hero crits (e.g. a performer-targeted self-buff) — a signature hook separate from the skill line.

limits.limit: Skill line can't hold a buff
limits.why: A combat_skill line cannot carry a buff-id or a stat modifier; there is no field for a resistance, conditional, or persistent stat on the line itself.
Exactly ONE of buff_ids / inline combat_stat_buff / buff_type / riposte per effect — the validator errors on more than one.
Inline .combat_stat_buff touches only the 10 combat stats and is unconditional; it cannot express resistances or any rule gate.
Effect and buff names hash-resolve at runtime; a misspelled .effect or .buff_ids token does nothing (no error outside debug).

forced.why: A camping skill IS a list of typed effect entries (buff / heal / stress_heal / remove_disease / reduce_torch...), each with a chance and target scope — payloads arrive through these entries, not on the skill root.
How many camping skills a hero gets is set by the hero's generation: block; a NET-NEW hero authors 2 class-specific plus shared, an OFFICIAL hero reuses vanilla and authors none.

choices.detail: A type:"buff" entry references buff ids, so it can carry any rule_type — though camp payoffs are usually plain unconditional party buffs.
type:"remove_disease" is the only in-dungeon disease-cure vector outside the Sanitarium; it respects each quirk's can_remove_with_camping_skill flag.
Each entry picks self / party target scope and a fire chance, letting one skill mix a self-heal, a party buff, and a torch cost.

limits.why: Vanilla camping can only remove diseases; there is no camping op to grant an ordinary quirk or negative.
The removal path clears diseases (is_disease quirks), not ordinary negative quirks; ordinary negatives need Sanitarium or a curio Purge.
Camping runs in the rest phase; it has none of the combat trigger hooks (on-hit, on-crit, round-end) that skills and trinkets expose.

forced.why: A trinket has no inline stat fields; every stat, resist or conditional it grants is a buff id in its buffs:[] list, which points at a buffs.json entry.
A trinket only exists in-game if it sits in a loot table with chances>0; rarity plus a private loot table is how it drops (and how you class-lock it out of the generic pool).

choices.detail: Two doors: buffs:[] applies stats passively while equipped, and any of the 22 <trigger>_additional_effects arrays fires effect lists on events (round_end, was_hit, on_kill, on_dodge...).

Each buffs:[] entry carries any rule_type (has_quirk, at_deaths_door, negative_quirk_above, monsterType, hpbelow...) plus is_false_rule — a fully conditional static trinket buff with no effect involved.
trigger_limit / quest_uses / transform_on_* / destroy_on_triggers_exhausted let a trinket expend charges, transform, or self-destroy across a quest.
Declaring a set_id ties this trinket to a set bonus that activates when 2+ members are equipped.

limits.why: A trinket cannot carry a loose .effect like a skill line; effects reach it only through the 22 trigger arrays or a carrier buff's attack_additional_effect_ids.
The all_/on_dodge family (idx 9,10,11,12,14,15,18) has the firing site inject the actor, so their effects MUST be authored .target target or the loader warns and mis-targets.

limits.limit: 'all_' is per-member, not a group apply
limits.why: kill_all_heroes and friends loop each living member and apply the effect individually; you cannot address the whole party as one group object.

forced.why: A set is literally { id, buffs:[...] }; its buff ids (source bsrc_trinket_set) are its only carried content, applied once 2+ members are equipped.
The bonus only fires when at least two equipped trinkets share the set_id; fewer than two makes the loader warn 'could not find 2 or more Trinkets'.

choices.detail: Every set buff can use any of the 93 stat_types with any rule_type, is_false_rule and duration/lifecycle keys — the ceiling is the whole buff system.
A carrier buff (may use a dummy stat_type at amount 0) with attack_additional_effect_ids is the only way a set fires a combat effect — on attack, any rule_type allowed.

limits.why: A set has none of the trinket entry's <trigger>_additional_effects, no transform/expend keys — no round_end, was_hit, on_dodge or on_quest_complete hooks.

limits.limit: On-attack is the only effect route
limits.why: The sole way to fire an effect from a set is a carrier buff's attack_additional_effect_ids; non-attack triggers must live on the member trinket entries instead.

forced.why: A quirk has no inline stat fields; its buffs:[] list of buff ids is the actual stat effect. A behavioral-only quirk carries empty buffs and relies on description plus engine handling.

choices.detail: Each quirk buff can carry any rule_type — the way to author 'a trait that only helps under condition X' (has_quirk, negative_quirk_above, actor_status...).
A non-empty curio_tag plus curio_tag_chance makes the hero compulsively interact with tagged curios (a 'mania'); keep_loot governs whether loot is kept.
is_positive and is_disease pick the slot pool; setting is_disease:true turns the same record into a disease with different caps and cure paths.
evolution_class_id, contagious_class_id, slot_size, roster_limit, use_item_changes and tags enable evolving/contagious/rare/slot-heavy quirks — still delivering power through buffs[].

limits.limit: Cannot carry or fire an effect
limits.why: A quirk has no trigger machinery; all conditional behavior must live in the buffs it references. Combat act-outs are a separate DLC-gated quirk_act_outs file, not the base record.
There are no inline stat fields on a quirk record; any modifier must be a buffs.json entry named in buffs:[].
A quirk is a delivery TARGET of other buses (curio, .disease effect, add_quirk activity, persist.roster); camping cannot grant one — only remove diseases.

forced.why: A disease is mechanically a quirk record with is_disease:true — same file, same buff model, only a different slot cap and cure paths.
Like quirks, the buffs:[] list holds the stat penalties directly; almost all diseases are unconditional negative stat buffs.

choices.detail: The .disease "<id>" effect field can be attached to any monster attack, hero skill or trap to inflict a specific disease (it actually accepts ANY quirk id; only .disease "any" is disease-filtered).
evolution_class_id plus evolution_duration_min/max auto-mutates the disease after N town-days; evolution_causes_death is optional (the CC vampirism chain).
contagious_class_id plus a roster.contagion.json block spreads the disease hero-to-hero across idle/building/activity contexts.
slot_size:3 (CC) fills all three disease slots with one disease, making it monopolize the hero's disease capacity.

limits.why: Like a quirk, the base disease record fires nothing on its own; only DLC use_item_dungeon_effects can trigger a combat effect on item use.
quirks_max_diseases is 3; a disease occupies the separate disease pool, not the 5 negative-quirk slots.
Diseases are cured via the Sanitarium disease_treatment activity or camping remove_disease (gated by can_remove_with_camping_skill), not ordinary negative-quirk treatment.

forced.why: The behavior lives in the deaths_door: record on the hero (or monster) .info — three engine-timed buff-id lists plus an optional enter-effects list.
.buffs, .recovery_buffs and .recovery_heart_attack_buffs are arbitrary buff-id lists; which list an id sits in decides its timing, and each id points at a buffs.json entry.

choices.detail: The three lists reach any buff, so DD can grant damage/crit/prot/dodge up instead of the vanilla ACC/DMG/SPD/SR penalties — a 'cornered animal' payoff.

.enter_effects fires effect names the moment the actor enters Death's Door (heal, cure DoTs, guard, party buff, damage, even summon), throttled by .enter_effect_round_cooldown; boot-test since no vanilla hero uses it.
Buff rule_types at_deaths_door and ondeathsdoorenter let a buff self-gate on DD state, stacking with list placement.

limits.why: You choose the buffs but not their timing — the engine applies each list at a fixed moment (held at DD / on recovery / after heart attack) by which list holds the id.
deathblow_chance, self/party stress pulses and NG+ death cap live in shared/rules.json (mode-level), not in the .info deaths_door: block.
The per-hero chance to die is the .death_blow resistance in the resistances: block, not a field of deaths_door:.

forced.why: An affliction/virtue is a trait_library.json entry that applies its buff ids while the resolve state is active; the stat/behavior payload is carried by those buffs.

choices.detail: Any buff on any carrier (skill, trinket, quirk) can self-gate on rule_type afflicted or virtued — giving a hero a distinct break-vs-steel payoff without touching trait_library.
Optional custom afflicted barks (<class>+str_afflicted_<state>) flavor the resolve state alongside its buffs.

limits.why: The base-game resolve state runs through the buff / compromised.json path and fires no effects; combat misbehavior needs the DLC quirk_act_outs file, not trait_library.
trait_library.json (afflictions/virtues) is a separate system from quirk_library.json despite the UI calling quirks 'traits'; you cannot author an affliction as a quirk.

forced.why: A monster defines its raw base stats and 8 combat resistances directly in stats:/resistances: — this stat authoring is required for the enemy to function.
combat_skill:/skill: fire effects by .effect name (same grammar as hero skills); anything the monster does beyond raw stats reaches buffs through those effects' .buff_ids.
A monster only shows up if it is placed in a region's encounter mash tables; placement is required but is not itself a buff or effect carrier.

choices.detail: Conditional behavior fires through reaction hooks: was_killed/was_hit effects (skill_reaction:), hp_reaction: phase triggers, death_reaction:, crit: .effects, spawn: .effects — the monster analog of trinket triggers.
A monster carries some buffs directly: companion: .buffs, battle_modifier hero/other-enemy buff instances, and mode: buffs are applied without an effect.
A free-form enemy_type: tag lets a hero '+% vs <type>' buff read it via rule_type monsterType — the monster<->hero pairing hook.
death_class:/shape_shifter: (transform), shared_health:/life_link: (multi-part), life_time: (expiring summons), captor_full/empty (capture) build bosses and summons.

limits.limit: AI brain is a reference only
limits.why: monster_brain: names an engine-provided brain; the desire/target logic is code-side and cannot be authored as a buff or effect — only tuned via battle_modifier/personality.
Anything conditional (on death, on hit, at 50% HP, on transform) must be a reaction hook, not a static buff; a plain buff has no event trigger.
The 20+ battle_modifier flags are boolean switches (targetability/surprise/stall/guard), not rule-gated buffs — no rule_type applies to them.

forced.why: Curios are CSV-driven at runtime (no JSON); the curio's power is a two-tier weighted RESULT table in curio_type_library.csv plus a curio_props.csv art row.
A curio carries no buff list; buffs arrive only via an Effect result naming an effect (its .buff_ids apply) or via a granted Quirk/Disease whose buffs apply (source bsrc_curio).

choices.detail: One curio block can weight Effect (fire effect/buff/inline DoT), Quirk (grant id or pos/neg bucket), Disease, Purge (clear a negative), Loot, Scouting or Summon.
A provision item (holy_water, skeleton_key, shovel, torch, medicinal_herbs...) used on the curio bypasses the whole default table and applies its own keyed row.
REGION FOUND selects a per-region result table, letting the same curio grant biome-specific quirks/loot; it selects results, not placement.
TAGS on the curio pair with a quirk's curio_tag so tagged heroes compulsively interact — the authoring side of manias.

limits.limit: No buff-id list of its own
limits.why: A curio cannot hold a buffs:[] field; every buff it grants is mediated by an Effect result or a granted quirk/disease.
The curio record has no rule gate; result selection is purely by weight, and REGION FOUND is a table selector, not a condition.
Shipped Purge results clear the negative-quirk bucket; there is no vanilla curio result that strips an enemy's or hero's positive buffs.

forced.why: A district grants power via typed DistrictXBuffData objects (e.g. DistrictHeroBuffData.buff_list is a direct buff-id list); an activity building grants via ops (apply_buff, add_quirk, add_trinket...).
A district buff_list[].type is STRICT-parsed — an unknown or misspelled DistrictXBuffData type is a guaranteed startup CTD (factory null-vtable call), so the 8 names must be copied byte-exact.

choices.detail: DistrictHeroBuffData with hero_type_tags grants buff ids only to matching-tagged heroes — the district-level gate for a class-specific persistent buff.
An activity's side_effects roll weighted results per completing hero: add_quirk, apply_buff, go_missing, add/remove_currency, activity_lock, add/remove_trinket.
DistrictCurioInteractionBuffData grants bonus stress-heal when a tagged hero uses a matching curio.

limits.why: Town carriers do not fire .effect names; their payloads are typed buff-data objects or activity ops with no effect-name path.
The add_trinket activity op grants a random trinket of a rarity; there is no field to grant a specific trinket id.
The district-buff factory caps at 64 registered classes; you cannot register more DistrictBuff types than the engine's table allows.

forced.why: actor_dot is an effect construct, not a top-level content type — it is authored as an effect: record with .actor_dot and update/duration timing on another carrier (skill, trinket trigger, monster reaction).
update_duration_type controls WHEN a tick fires (per turn, after_turn_attack, after_turn_attack_kill), defining the timer/ramp/punish schedule.

choices.detail: Each tick or the completion/kill transition can fire further effects (stun, ramp buff, loot-mule summon) which reach rule-gated buffs via .buff_ids.
.dotBleed/.dotBlight/.dotBurn choose which resistance applies; .health_damage deals raw damage with no resist.
Common uses: delayed-stun sigil, forever-ramp corruption, self-repairing immobilize, guaranteed on-kill loot mule, target-triggered punish burn.

limits.why: actor_dot cannot exist on its own; it is a wiring pattern that must live inside an effect authored on a real carrier.

limits.limit: No buff-id list on a non-effect record
limits.why: It reaches buffs only the normal effect way (its own .buff_ids); it is a carrier because it fires payloads on a schedule, not because it holds buffs.

forced.why: The stance is flipped by a .set_mode effect fired from a skill (optionally gated on hit/miss/chance); the register changes only through this effect.
Per-stance stats come from buffs gated on rule_type in_mode (with is_false_rule to invert) — the stance state itself carries no stat.

choices.detail: Skills carry .valid_modes so a builder is available only in certain stances; slicing builders this way encodes mode wheels, heat gauges or combo ladders.
A sub-100% .chance on set_mode, or .on_hit/.on_miss variants, makes an accuracy-gated or random stance shift.
A mode: block can carry battle_start_effect_ids and (for afflictions) affliction_combat_skill_id; monsters run the same FSM.

limits.why: set_mode sets an exact mode, not a relative step; N rungs of a ladder require N duplicated skill lines — there is no increment operator.
A mode/stance is a creative primitive built from vanilla parts (set_mode + .valid_modes + in_mode); there is no dedicated stance content type.

forced.why: A summoned actor must exist as a real monster .info to be referenced; the summon effect names its base class id.
Heroes and monsters reach summons only through effect fields (spawn_target_actor_base_class_id / summon_monsters) on a skill or reaction.

choices.detail: companion: .buffs is a direct per-turn buff-id list applied to the paired partner, plus .heal_per_turn_percent — a rare direct-buff monster field.
A summoned actor's spawn: .effects fire on spawn, running effect logic the caster can't (the invisible-executor / self-killing loot-mule patterns).
life_time: .alive_round_limit auto-kills a temporary summon after N rounds.

limits.limit: No summon without a monster record
limits.why: You cannot summon an ad-hoc actor; the referenced class must be a defined monster .info or the reference fails.

limits.limit: controller stress is a plain field
limits.why: controller: .stress_per_controlled_turn is a numeric field, not a rule-gated buff — it cannot carry conditions.
